div.div:
1 زَاتَهُ , aor. يَزِيتُهُ, [inf. n. زَيْتٌ,] He anointed him, or it, with زَيْت, i. e. oil of the زَيْتُون [or olive]. (Msb.) You say, زِتٌّ, meaning I anointed my head, and the head of another, with oil of the زيتون. (L.) ―
-b2- And زِتُّهُ, (Lh, S, K,) aor. أَزِيتُهُ, (S, K, TA, in the CK اَزِتُّه, and so in my MS. copy of the K,) inf. n. زَيْتٌ, (K,) I put زَيْت [i. e. olive-oil] into it; namely, the food; (S, K;) or the crumbled bread: or I prepared it therewith: (TA:) or I moistened it, or stirred it about, or moistened and mixed it, with زيت; namely, bread, and crumbled bread. (Lh, TA.) ―
-b3- And زَاتَهُمْ (Lh, S, K, TA, in the CK [erroneously] زَأَتَهُمْ) He fed them with زَيْت: (Lh, K:) or he made زيت to be the seasoning of their food. (S.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
